high.title: Markets Advance Optimistic with Peace Negotiations; Oil Falls and Ibovespa in Dollar Terms Rises Today (14)
high.summary: Global markets are advancing on Tuesday (14th) while oil prices retreat, reflecting relief from easing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. The movement gained momentum after US President Donald Trump indicated openness to resume negotiations with Iran, reinforcing expectations of a more consistent ceasefire in the region. According to Bloomberg sources, Washington and Tehran are discussing the possibility of new negotiation rounds to extend the two-week truce signed on April 7th, which expires in the coming days. Despite the more conciliatory tone, the US maintains pressure on Iran through a naval blockade limiting vessel entry and exit from Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz. This development is crucial for FX and bond traders as reduced geopolitical tensions typically support risk assets like Brazilian equities and could strengthen BRL against USD. Lower oil prices also ease inflationary pressures, potentially supporting BCB's dovish monetary policy stance and Selic rate cuts.

high.title: Ibovespa at 196 Thousand Points: 'It Won't Take Much Effort to Reach 200 Thousand Points', Says Analyst; See 10 Stocks to Buy Now
high.summary: For the third consecutive trading session, the Ibovespa continues to defy the macroeconomic scenario and set new highs, touching 197,554 points on Friday (10th). The index has already risen 4% this week despite an unstable environment for risk assets. The resilience comes despite the closure of the Strait of Hormuz impacting interest rate cut expectations and Selic policy. IBGE released March IPCA inflation data showing acceleration to 0.88%, representing a 0.18 percentage point increase from February (0.70%) and above market projections of 0.77%. Empiricus Research analyst Ruy Hungria views the Ibovespa's performance amid this turbulence as a clear signal of underlying strength. The index's ability to reach new highs despite inflationary pressures and geopolitical tensions suggests strong domestic fundamentals. For equity investors, the analyst's prediction of reaching 200,000 points indicates continued bullish momentum, though higher inflation readings could pressure BCB to maintain hawkish policy stance.

medium.title: Vale (VALE3) Shares May Unlock More Value Thanks to a Little-Known 'Crown Jewel', According to Analyst
medium.summary: Vale (VALE3) closed March down 6.77% but still accumulates a 14.6% gain in 2026 after rising 49% in 2025. Empiricus analyst Ruy Hungria views the decline as profit-taking given resilient iron ore prices and possible commodity rotation toward oil due to geopolitical tensions. The analyst believes Vale has an underappreciated "crown jewel" that could drive shares to attractive levels, benefiting from dollar revenues amid currency uncertainty.

medium.title: With War, Inflation and Stock Market Records: Where to Invest Now? See Best Recommendations in Money Picks
medium.summary: After the ceasefire announcement between US and Iran, the Brazilian stock index hit another record this year, surpassing 190,000 points, though the scenario remains unpredictable. The Strait of Hormuz closure elevated global tensions, pressuring supply chains, oil prices, and inflation, raising doubts about Brazil's interest rate cut pace and Ibovespa's future. Empiricus highlights a new Brazilian commodities ETF for diversified exposure to oil, metals, and agribusiness sectors.
